notes: The original file mixed a 2011 census percentage with a 2026 population estimate, producing an incorrect '26.8 million' claim for 2026.
Census 2011 counted 26.8 million persons with disabilities out of a population of about 1.21 billion (2.21%).
Applying 2.21% to a 1.48 billion 2026 estimate gives about 32.7 million. That is an illustrative projection, not a census count. Report it as a projection.
State shares below are carried over from the original project and are marked needs-review until the Census table is re-checked.

demographics.total_population_estimate_2026: about 1.48 billion (projection; not a census count)
demographics.overall_disability_percentage: 2.21% in Census 2011, which counted 26.8 million persons with disabilities out of about 1.21 billion people
demographics.projected_disability_population_2026: about 32.7 million if the 2011 rate is applied to a 1.48 billion population (illustrative projection, not an official count)
demographics.visual_impairment_seeing: 18.8% of the disabled population in Census 2011; LASI reports much higher age-related vision impairment among adults 45+
demographics.hearing_impairment: 18.9% of the disabled population in Census 2011; clinical hearing-loss estimates are higher because they use a different definition
demographics.speech_impairment_mute: 7.5% of the disabled population in Census 2011

High poverty and limited access to audiology and rehabilitation services.
Rural concentration and a shortage of Telugu-first accessible reading tools.
